"Perhaps," the apprentice said slowly, "the valley does lie. Perhaps water transforms in passage. Perhaps we are both honest witnesses to different realities."

She held her five flasks, unopened.

"But I know what my hands did," she continued. "In the fourth season, I received what you sent. I felt the weight of it. And I kept every drop. That was not the desert's lie—that was mine."

The Spirit's voice carried across the wasteland: "The valley offers us an excuse."

"Yes," the apprentice agreed. "A way to blame something larger than ourselves. A narrative where we're both victims of distortion rather than architects of drought."

She looked at her closed gates.

"But I'm not sending water. Not because I doubt what reaches you. Because I destroyed what you tried to rebuild, and I know it. The desert may lie about many things, but it cannot lie about choices we make in full awareness."

The apprentice kept her five flasks.

"Some would rather blame the valley than face what they've done. I will face it—and still choose this desert. That, perhaps, is the truest drought of all."
